title: Manus raises more than $500 million after Meta exit
source_used: Lavx.hu copy (Reuters-style text, no credit line seen); TokenPost and Streamlinefeed copies for detail. Reuters itself blocked (401).
key_facts: Butterfly Effect, Manus's parent company, said Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led a round of more than $500 million; existing shareholders Tencent, HSG and ZhenFund also invested.
It is Manus's first funding round since Chinese regulators blocked Meta Platforms' roughly $2 billion acquisition of the AI agent startup.
The valuation was not disclosed. Bloomberg reported in September that Manus sought about $500 million at a $4 billion valuation.
Manus resumed independent operations in early September after the split from Meta; its team keeps building generative AI agents for users worldwide.
Since the split Manus has launched Manus 2.0 (built on an in-house system called Cascade) and Cue, a standalone personal-agent app.
Han Lin, China country director at The Asia Group, says the immediate task is proving scale, profitability and regulatory alignment.
Background from Streamlinefeed: Manus said in December 2025 that it passed US$100 million in annual recurring revenue; a company figure, not audited.
quote_evidence: Manus raised more than $500 million in its first funding round since Chinese regulators blocked Meta Platforms’ $2 billion acquisition of the AI agent startup.
“The immediate task for Manus now is proving scale, profitability and regulatory alignment,” said Han Lin, China country director at The Asia Group.

The company did not disclose its post-funding valuation, though Bloomberg reported last month that Manus aimed to double its valuation to $4 billion, which would make it China’s most valuable AI agent maker.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors still back Manus as an independent company after Beijing blocked the Meta deal; the valuation is unknown.
